issue_context.title: Use TaskToApm everywhere
issue_context.body:
We should be using TaskToApm on all streams for the BeginWrite, EndWrite, BeginRead, and EndRead apis. A few places where we don't:
- https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/Middleware/ResponseCompression/src/ResponseCompressionBody.cs
- https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/52eff90fbcfca39b7eb58baad597df6a99a542b0/src/Servers/HttpSys/src/ResponseStream.cs#L77
- https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/52eff90fbcfca39b7eb58baad597df6a99a542b0/src/Middleware/ResponseCaching/src/Streams/ResponseCachingStream.cs#L184
- https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/52eff90fbcfca39b7eb58baad597df6a99a542b0/src/Middleware/ResponseCaching/src/Streams/SegmentWriteStream.cs#L194

As an example: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/52eff90fbcfca39b7eb58baad597df6a99a542b0/src/Servers/HttpSys/src/RequestProcessing/ResponseBody.cs#L525

review_comments:
The async-version has the same code-path, so this removal should be OK in terms of correctness.

But with this change it may allocate more.
The async version needs to allocate a `RequestStreamAsyncResult` too, plus there's the `Task`-object.

I don't have any feeling if / how this method is called and used, so this may not be a concern at all.

But while looking at the code for `RequestStreamAsyncResult` I saw the TCS, which could replaced by a non-allocating variant --> https://github.com/gfoidl/aspnetcore/commit/e11e537c49fee94c4abcaf656841e2f34c6e7645
Is this something to pursue? (Maybe in a separate issue / PR).

Removing the redundant code is likely for the best.

Feel free to follow-up about the TCS in a different PR.
